assertions: The ship is living and not sunk: she is not wrecked or totally lost, and the repeated reports of her wreck are false or greatly exaggerated

She did meet real danger and battering on the voyage and has taken some harm or strain to her hull or gear (Saturn in Aries square the Cancer Ascendant, very near), enough to need repair, but her hull is essentially sound and she has not gone down
She is near land and in or close to a safe harbour or anchorage, riding at anchor rather than lost in the open sea
Her position is to the south-west of London, towards and on or near her destination coast, the coast of Spain
The ship's company/crew are essentially safe, the Moon being exalted and close to Jupiter

The voyage and its profit are delayed and impaired, with some loss or extra cost on the venture (South Node in the 9th and Saturn afflicting the Ascendant), but the cargo and venture are not wholly lost

Certain news of her safety will come very soon, within a few days and in any case within about a week of the question, because the Moon applies by trine to Mercury, significator of tidings, wanting only a few minutes of the exact trine
The news will be good news confirming that she is safe, arriving by letter or messenger from partners or correspondents abroad (Mercury in the 7th, in reception with Mars)
method: Lilly horary astrology for a ship at sea (Christian Astrology, Book II rules), using the chart positions given in the question
reasoning: Ship is signified by the Cancer Ascendant (her bulk/body) and its lady the Moon. The Moon is in Taurus in her exaltation in the 11th, essentially very strong, near the body of benefic Jupiter, and applying by an almost exact trine (wanting a few minutes) to the Sun and to Mercury in the 7th: a strong, well-aspected significator cannot denote a ship sunk, so the wreck rumours fail. Saturn in Aries in the 11th casting a close square to the Ascendant and the South Node in the 9th show the real danger, battering, delay and loss on the long voyage, but these afflict without destroying because the Moon's dignity and benefic application outweigh them. The Moon in a fixed earth sign, moving to planets in the western 7th, places her near land at anchor in a haven in the south-western direction of her Spanish destination. Timing is taken in days because the question is about imminent tidings and the Moon-Mercury trine lacks only minutes of perfection: news is therefore a matter of a few days, brought by Mercury in the 7th in reception with Mars, dispositor of the Part of Fortune.
summary: The ship is alive and safe in or near a harbour on the Spanish coast to the south-west, battered but not wrecked, and confirming news of her will arrive within a few days.
